Functional-clock cycles SCL is held HIGH per bit (I2C-bus spec t_HIGH minimum). For 100kHz with a 32MHz AHB input clock and clkdiv=2 (16MHz/62.5ns functional clock), program 64 (t_HIGH=4000ns min).
Functional-clock cycles SCL is held LOW per bit (I2C-bus spec t_LOW minimum). For 100kHz with a 32MHz AHB input clock and clkdiv=2 (16MHz/62.5ns functional clock), program 76 (t_LOW=4700ns min).
START condition hold time (t_HD;STA), in functional-clock cycles. For 100kHz with a 32MHz AHB input clock and clkdiv=2, program 64 (4000ns min).
STOP condition setup time (t_SU;STO), in functional-clock cycles. For 100kHz with a 32MHz AHB input clock and clkdiv=2, program 64 (4000ns min).
Minimum bus-free time between a STOP and the next START (t_BUF), in functional-clock cycles. For 100kHz with a 32MHz AHB input clock and clkdiv=2, program 76 (4700ns min).
Repeated-START setup time (t_SU;STA), in functional-clock cycles. For 100kHz with a 32MHz AHB input clock and clkdiv=2, program 76 (4700ns min).

Maximum functional-clock cycles the master allows a slave to stretch SCL before flagging clkstretch_timeout. Independent of I2C_SPEED -- leave at reset default (40000 cycles) for 100kHz/32MHz-AHB/clkdiv=2, or size to a desired timeout via ceil(timeout_us*1000/T_func_ns).

Maximum functional-clock cycles this slave may itself stretch SCL before flagging clkstretch_timeout. Independent of I2C_SPEED -- leave at reset default (100000 cycles) for 100kHz/32MHz-AHB/clkdiv=2, sized the same way as mst_max_clkstretch_cnt.

Maximum functional-clock cycles SCL may be held low by an external device before flagging smbus_timeout. Independent of I2C_SPEED -- leave at reset default (140000 cycles) for 100kHz/32MHz-AHB/clkdiv=2, or size to the desired SMBus timeout (e.g. 25-35ms) via ceil(timeout_us*1000/T_func_ns).
